newsitem.title: USA: Dollar mixed in light pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar mixed in light pre-holiday trade.

text.p: The dollar drifted higher against the German mark but fell against the Japanese yen in light trading Monday as the Christmas and New Year's holidays drew nigh.

"It feels like it's time for Christmas," said Mark Gargano, managing director of currency derivatives at First Union National Bank. "Whatever you've done for the year, people are sort of closing out their books."
U.S. stock and bond markets will close early on Tuesday and remain closed Wednesday for the Christmas holiday.
Foreign exchange flows are also expected to wind down early Tuesday, with traders taking the day off on Wednesday.
Tom Benfer, director of foreign exchange at the Bank of Montreal, noted that some U.S. companies are bringing money home from their subsidiaries as dividends are being declared.
"So, they generally are selling currencies and buying U.S. dollars," Benfer said. "That's probably what's giving the dollar a little bit of a boost here."
The dollar crept to a high of 1.5565 marks before trading at 1.5545 marks in late trading, up from 1.5515 late Friday.
Sellers emerged when the dollar hit its peak for the day against the mark. "We just had an order to sell about 50 (million) bucks when it was up there," one trader said.
"Usually, an order like that would be swallowed up (but) it actually moved the market."
The dollar fell to 114.08 yen late Monday from 114.27 yen late Friday.

The British pound rose as minutes from the Oct. 30 monthly monetary policy meeting between Bank of England Governor Eddie George and Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke seemed to hint that recent rate hikes might not be enough to contain latent inflation pressures in Britain.
Mike Malpede, a senior foreign exchange analyst at Refco Group Ltd., contended it is just a question of timing before the next rate rise.
"I think the trade will be looking at the Jan. 15 meeting as the next time frame. So, sterling should be well supported," he said.
The British pound rose to $1.6775 from $1.6725.
The dollar rose to 1.3373 Swiss francs from 1.3345 late Thursday. It fell to Canadian $1.3666 from $1.3681.
